frame.text: We used a bounded queue between ingestion workers and the feature store writer. At the high-water mark the producer blocked, propagating backpressure to the HTTP handler which shed load with a 429. Consumer lag was the alerting signal because lag rises before throughput drops.

payload.question_intent: Evaluate understanding of system design mechanisms for backpressure handling, load shedding, and monitoring in streaming ingestion pipelines.
payload.verdict_summary: You gave a crisp, accurate, and mechanism-focused explanation of backpressure propagation and alerting strategies. You clearly articulated how bounded queues prevent memory exhaustion and how lag serves as a leading indicator over throughput. To make it a perfect 10, you could briefly touch on client-side retry handling for shed requests.

spans.excerpt: We used a bounded queue between ingestion workers and the feature store writer.
spans.explanation: Using a bounded queue prevents unbounded memory growth under producer-consumer speed imbalances.

spans.excerpt: At the high-water mark the producer blocked, propagating backpressure to the HTTP handler which shed load with a 429.
spans.explanation: Correctly describes synchronous backpressure propagation returning an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response to upstream clients.

spans.excerpt: Consumer lag was the alerting signal because lag rises before throughput drops.
spans.explanation: Accurately identifies consumer lag as a leading indicator of performance degradation before downstream throughput drops.

ideal_answer_outline: Explain the queue architecture (bounded channel) and backpressure trigger conditions (high-water mark).
Detail the propagation mechanism from worker to HTTP layer leading to HTTP 429 load shedding.
Mention client handling strategies (exponential backoff and jitter) to avoid thundering herd.
Explain monitoring signals, contrasting early indicators (consumer lag) with late indicators (throughput drops).
payload.followup_probe: How did your client applications handle those 429 responses to prevent a thundering herd when retrying?
